newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds end mixed in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds end mixed in quiet trade.

text.p: Canadian bonds ended Monday's trading mixed, slightly down in the long and short end, but narrowly stronger in the middle of the curve, dealers said.
They said Canadian bonds partly recovered from losses last week on comments by Fed chairman Alan Greenspan, because of a flight to quality from European Monetary Union countries.
Investors bought U.S. and Canadian dollar investments, driven by speculation that the EMU was floundering.
Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer failed to staunch the trickle into dollar-backed investments by saying speculation about the EMU timetable was "wrong".
Canada's 30-year bond was down C$0.01 to 111.34 to yield 7.084 percent, while the 10-year benchmark was up C$0.03 at 104.28 to yield 6.40 percent.
Traders said the bonds recovered slightly from negative comments made by Greenspan last week, analysts said.
But both Canadian and U.S. bonds were expected to remain under pressure from a negative bias ahead of Greenspan's further testimony before Congress on Wednesday.
Also weighing on bonds was a report from the National Association of Purchasing Management on Monday, which hinted at a rise in inflation.
The overall NAPM index rose to 53.1 in February from 52.0 in January, while the prices index rose to 55.1 from 51.4.
Traders said bonds recovered somewhat from a weak opening on Monday on the basis of a flight to quality from European Monetary Union countries.
